State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Harish Kumar Dewangan vs Smt.Sarita Bajpai & Ors. on 12 September, 2016
CHHATTISGARH STATE
 CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
 PANDRI, RAIPUR (C.G.)

 Complaint Case No.CC/2016/14
 Instituted on : 08.04.2016

Harish Kumar Dewangan, Aged 38 years,
S/o Shri Horilal Dewangan,
R/o : Village, Post & Police Station Gunderdehi,
District Balod (C.G.). ... Complainant.

 Vs.

1. Smt. Sarita Bajpai, Aged about 42 years,
W/o Late Sanjay Kumar Bajpai,
Present Administrator and Heir - Husband
Sanjay Bajpai and Sanjay Bajpai Builders Pvt. Ltd.
Address : Third Floor, Krishna Complex,
Kutchery Chowk, Raipur (C.G.)
Other address Shankar Nagar, Raipur (C.G.).

2. Yogeshwar Shukla, Aged about 45 years,
Director and Administrator - Sanjay Bajpai Builders
Private Limited,
Address : Office Third Floor, Krishna Complex,
Kutchery Chowk, Raipur (C.G.)

3. Sanjay Bajpai Builders Pvt. Ltd.
Address - Office Third Floor, Krishna Complex,
Kutchery Chowk, Raipur (C.G.) ... Opposite Parties

PRESENT: -

HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE R.S. SHARMA, PRESIDENT
HON'BLE SHRI D.K. PODDAR, MEMBER

COUNSEL FOR THE PARTIES:

Shri S. Pandya, for the complainant.
Shri K.K. Shukla, for the opposite parties.
 // 2 //

 ORDER
Dated : 12/09/2016
 PER :- HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE R.S. SHARMA, PRESIDENT.

 The complainant filed this consumer complaint under
Section

17
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 against the OPs seeking

following reliefs :-
(a) To direct the OPs to pay a sum of Rs.22,35,000/- (Rupees

 Twenty Two Lakhs Thirty Five Thousand) to the

 complainant, which was paid by the complainant to the

 OPs, along with interest @ 24% p.a. from 30.10.2012.
(b) To direct the OPs to pay a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees Five

 Lakhs) to the complainant towards compensation for mental

 agony.
(c) To direct the OPs to pay a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty

 Thousand) to the complainant towards cost of litigation

 along with interest @ 18% p.a.
(d) To grant any other relief, which this Commission deems fit.
2. Briefly stated the facts of the complaint of the complainant are

that the OPs published an advertisement to the effect that in Village

Sejbahar, P.H.No.119/50 a project was approved by the Town and

Country Planning Department, Raipur for construction of colony. On

being influenced with the advertisement published by the OPs, the
 // 3 //

complainant purchased 3000 sq ft. situated at New Swagat Vihar Plot

No.425 Phase - 4, Village Dunda at the rate of Rs.745/- per sq. ft. The

complainant deposited a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- through cheque

No.002211 dated 27.09.2012, a sum of Rs.8,33,000/- through cheque

No.002212 dated 26.10.2012, Rs.5,67,000/- through cheque No.002213

dated 27.10.2012, a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- through DD No.725710

0000020000 00025816 dated 26.10.2012 and Rs.1,35,000/- through

cheque No.121457 dated 30/10/2012. The complainant deposited

total amount of Rs.22,35,000/- with Sanjay Bajpai Colonizer and

Developers. Sanjay Bajpai Colonizer and Developers gave receipts for

the above amount deposited by the complainant. The complainant

continuously made contact with Sanjay Bajpai for execution of sale

deed and Sanjay Bajpai told him that the lay out was approved by

Town and Country Planning, Raipur, but the site was not developed.

The OPs made pretext for near about 1 ½ years. In the month of April,

2014, the complainant came to know through newspaper that land of

Phase 4 of the Project at Village Dunda is government land and the

government has cancelled the approval given by the Town and

Country Planning Department, Raipur and the matter is pending

before the Court. The complainant met with Sanjay Bajpai. Sanjay

Bajpai Builders Private Limited executed an agreement with the

complainant on 26.05.2014 and promised that if the judgment in

respect of New Swagat Vihar Phase 4 is not come within 6 months,
 // 4 //

then the Company will execute sale deed in favour of the

complainant without taking any additional fees. All amenities like

road, drainage, electric poll will be arranged by the Company within

six months and if the judgment is not come within 6 months then the

amount will be refunded to the complainant with adequate

compensation. The case is still pending before the Court and OPs have

not executed sale deed in favour of the complainant. Even the amount

deposited by the complainant has not been refunded. Sanjay Bajpai

Builders Pvt. Ltd. has deliberately and with malafide intention sold the

land to the complainant, which was not in its ownership and gave false

and misleading representation to the complainant. The OPs gave false

assurance to the complainant to refund the amount, but they did not

refund the amount to the complainant and committed deficiency in

service and unfair trade practice. Hence this complaint. The

complainant is entitled to get reliefs as prayed by him in the relief

clause of the complaint.
3. The OPs have filed their joint written statement and averred

that Sanjay Bajpai was active director of Sanjay Bajpai Builders

Private Limited and was performing all works of the O.P.No.3. The

O.P.No.3 obtained approval from Town and Country Planning

Department regarding Swagat Vihat Phase 1 and other Phases. The

plot in question was sold by the O.P. No.3 through its director Sanjay

Bajpai to the complainant and an agreement was executed in favour
 // 5 //

of the complainant on 26.05.2014. The agreement dated 26.05.2014 is

illegal and is not executable and contract is void. O.P.No.1 Smt. Sarita

Bajpai is widow of Sanjay Baipai. She is not an active director or

partner of Sanjay Bajpai Builders Private Limited and Sarita Bajpai is

not personally liable for the act of Sanjay Bajpai and she is only a

sleeping director of Sanjay Bajpai Builders Private Limited. The

complainant has not purchased 3000 sq ft. plot i.e. Plot No.425 situated

at Village Dunda @ Rs.745/- per sq. ft. and he also did not paid a sum

of Rs.22,35,000/- to the builder. Sanjay Bajpai was principal director

of Sanjay Bajpai Builders Pvt. Ltd, therefore, Crime No.120/2013 was

registered against him at Police Station, Moudhapara, Raipur for

offence under
Sections 420
,
467
,
468
,
471
,
120
IPC and under
Section 2
of Power of Attorney Act, Rule 16-17 of Land Development Rule 1984

and under
Section 5
,
322
,
323
,
542
and
628
of Companies Act. . Crime

No.187/2013 for offence under
Section 420
,
467
,
468
,
471
and
120B
IPC

was registered against him by Police Station, Gole Bazar, Raipur and

Crime No.200/2013 for offence under
Sections 420
,
467
,
468
was

registered against him by Police Station, Gole Bazar and three separate

charge sheet were filed before Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur,

therefore, the O.P.No.1 and O.P.No.2 are not liable for the criminal act

committed by Sanjay Bajpai. Sanjay Bajpai executed an agreement on

26.05.2014 with the complainant, which is against the law and the

government cancelled the Swagat Vihar Project, therefore, agreement
 // 6 //

executed in favour of the complainant, is void and is not executable.

The complaint is not maintainable before this Commission. The matter

relates to licence and approval given by Town and Country Planning

Department and the matter is pending before Hon'ble Chhattisgarh

High Court, Bilaspur. The agreement executed between the parties is

conditional agreement. The complainant is having remedy to seek

relief from Civil Court, therefore, the complainant is not entitled to get

any relief from this Commission and the complaint is liable to be

dismissed.
4. The complainant has filed documents. Ex.P/1 is brochure,

Ex.P/2 is receipt No.1690 dated 27.09.2012, Ex.P/3 is receipt No.166

dated 25.10.2012, Ex.P/4 is receipt No.1710 dated 25.10.2012, Ex.P/5 is

receipt No.1711 dated 30.10.2012, Ex.P/5 is receipt No.168 dated

30.12.2012, Ex.P/7 is Sale Deed dated 26.05.2014, Ex.P.8 is legal notice

dated 02.03.21016 sent to OPs, Ex.P/9 are postal receipts, Ex.P.10 are

acknowledgements, Ex.P/11 is public notice issued by Sanjay Bajpai in

the newspaper.
5. The OPs have filed Final Report of Crime No.170/2-013 P.S.

Gole Bazar, Raipur.
6. Shri S.Pandya, learned counsel appearing for the complainant

has argued that the complainant purchased 3000 sq ft. plot i.e. plot

No.425 situated at New Swagat Vihar Phase - 4, Village Dunda @
 // 7 //

Rs.745/- per sq. ft. and paid a sum of Rs.22,35,000/- to the O.P.No.3,

but the OPs did not construct the house and did not give the

possession of the house to the complainant. Even the amount which

was deposited by the complainant has not been refunded, therefore,

the complainant is consumer and the OPs are service provider. Sanjay

Bajpai Builders Private Limited executed an agreement with the

complainant on 26.05.2014. In agreement Sanjay Bajpai admitted that a

sum of Rs.22,35,000/- was received by Sanjay Bajpai Builders Private

Limited from the complainant and he also promised that if the

judgment in respect of New Swagat Vihar Phase 4 is not come within

6 months, then the Company will execute sale deed in favour of the

complainant without taking any additional fees. All amenities like

road, drainage, electric poll will be arranged by the Company within

six months and if the judgment is not come within 6 months then the

amount will be refunded to the complainant with adequate

compensation. Sanjay Bajpai Builders Private Limited is service

provider and O.P.No.1 Smt. Sarita Bajpai is director of said Company

and at present she is administrator of Sanjay Bajpai Builders Private

Limited and O.P.No.2 Yogeshwar Shukla is director and administrator

of the said company, therefore after death of Sanjay Bajpai, the

O.P.No.1 and O.P.No.2 are active directors of the said company and

they are equally liable for act committed by Sanjay Bajpai. According

to terms and conditions of the agreement the house was not
 // 8 //

constructed within stipulated period and amount deposited by the

complainant was not refunded, therefore, the OPs committed

deficiency in service.
The OPs neither refunded the money nor

delivered the possession of house to the complainant, which comes in

the category of deficiency in service. The OPs did construct the house

and also did not obey terms and conditions of the agreement and

amount was not refunded to the complainant, therefore, the

complainant entitled to get the deposited amount along with interest @

24% p.a from 30.10.2012 till realisation. The complainant suffered

mental agony, therefore, he is entitled for Rs.5,00,000/- towards

compensation for mental agony and Rs.50,000/- towards cost of

litigation. He placed reliance on
Perin Bazun Dittia & Anr. Vs. Emaar

Hills Township Pvt. Ltd. III
(2016) CPJ 67 (NC);
Navin Khanna (Dr.)

& Ors. Vs. Unitech Reliable Projects Pvt. Ltd. III
(2016) CPJ 203 (NC);

M/s Vyas Enterprises Through its Proprietor, Sh. Mahendra

Jayantilal Vyas Vs. Das Darshan Co-operative Housing Society Ltd.,

2014 (3) CPR 169 (NC);
Narne Estates Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. Vs. Amitabh

Bhattacharya & Ors. II
(2016) CPJ 284 (NC); Punjab Urban Planning

& Development Authority through its Chief Administrator & Anr.

Vs. Sh. Atmanand Jain Shabha (Regd.) 2013 (4) CPR 584 (NC);
Ghaziabad Development Authority Vs. Balbir Singh
2013 (4) CPR

405 (SC);
Rainbow Realtors Vs. Solomon Esau David Through LRS
.
II (2010) CPJ 265 (NC);
Ansal Properties & Infrastructure Ltd. Vs.

Nidhi Jain & Ors.
, 2013 (3) CPR 144 (NC); Sh. Vinod Kumar Goyal
 // 9 //

Vs. M/s. Mera Baba Real Estate Pvt. Ltd. 2013 (4) CPR 817 (NC); Shri

Satish Kumar Pandey and Anr. Vs. M/s. UNITECH Ltd., Through its

Managing Director 2015 (2) CPR 709 (NC); Ansal Housing &

Construction Ltd. & Ors. Vs. Birender Singh Yadav II (2016) CPJ 289

(NC) and M/s.
S.S. Construction & Anr. Vs. Mr. Mathew Varghese

Through
its Power of Attorney Holder 2013 (3) CPR 545 (NC).
7. Shri K.K. Shukla, learned counsel appearing for the OPs has

argued that the complainant is not consumer and O.P.No.1 &

O.P.No.2 are not active directors of Sanjay Bajpai Builders Private

Limited and agreement was executed by Sanjay Bajpai in his personal

capacity, therefore, the O.P.No.1 and O.P.No.2 are not liable for any

criminal act committed by Sanjay Bajpai and agreement executed in

favour of the complainant, is not void and is not executable. The

complainant is only having remedy to file civil suit for recovery of

amount. This Commission has no jurisdiction to take cognizance in

the matter, therefore, the complaint is liable to be dismissed.
8. We have heard learned counsel appearing for both the parties
and have also perused the documents filed by the parties.
9. Shri K.K. Shukla, learned counsel appearing for the OPs has

contended that O.P.No.1 Smt. Sarita Bajpai and O.P.No.2 Yogeshwar

Shukla are sleeping directs of Sanjay Bajpai Builders Private Limited.

The above contention is not acceptable. The complainant specifically
 // 10 //

pleaded that at present the O.P.No.1 Smt. Sarita Bajpai and O.P.No.2

Yogeshwar Shukla are directors and administrators of Sanjay Bajpai

Builders Private Limited. The complainant has filed copy of charge

sheet filed against Sanjay Bajpai before Judicial Magistrate First Class,

Raipur. On investigation, the Police found that Sanjay Bajpai and

Smt. Sarita Bajpai both are directors of Sanjay Bajpai Builders Private

Limited and they obtained licence in respect of Village Boria Kala

P.H.No.117/53, Tahsil and District Raipur for total land measuring

24.971 hectare. In revenue case No47/A/89(A) 2009-10 also, the

licence was issued in favour of Sanjay Bajpai Builder Private Limited,

Director Sanjay Bajpai in respect of Village Boria Kala for total land

measuring 20.581 hectare. It appears that O.P.No.1 Smt. Sarita Bajpai is

an active director along with Sanjay Baipai, Director of Sanjay Bajpai

Builders Private Limited.
10. The complainant pleaded that he paid amount of Rs.22,35,000/-

to the O.P. No.3. The complainant has filed copy of Agreement dated

26.05.2014 executed between Sanjay Bajapi and Harish Kumar

Dewangan (the complainant). In the said agreement, Sanjay Bajpai

admitted that he has received a sum of Rs.22,35,000/- from the

complainant for Plot No.425 measuring 3000 Sq ft. situated at New

Swagat Vihar Phase - 4, Village Dunda. In the agreement it is

mentioned that :-

11. From bare perusal of the agreement it appears that Sanjay

Bajpai Builders Private Limited executed an agreement with the

complainant on 26.05.2014 and promised that if the judgment in

respect of New Swagat Vihar Phase 4 ,is not come within 6 months,

then the Company will execute sale deed in favour of the

complainant without taking any additional fees. All amenities like

road, drainage, electric poll will be arranged by the Company within

six months and if the judgment is not come within 6 months then the
 // 12 //

amount will be refunded to the complainant with adequate

compensation. As the judgment has not come within stipulated

period, therefore, the complainant is entitled for the refund of the

amount deposited by him with the OPs. The OPs received the amount

from the complainant for construction of house and the after

construction of the house, the possession of the house was not handed

over by the OPs to the complainant. The possession of the house was

required to be handed over to the complainant by the OPs, but no

construction of house was carried out, therefore, the OPs are service

provider and the complainant is consumer of the OPs.
12. Now we shall examine whether the complainant is entitled to

get interest on the deposited amount @ 24% p.a. ?
13.
In
Bhupinder Singh Vs. Unitech Ltd.
2016(3) CLT 343,

Hon'ble National Commission has observed that house was not

constructed and possession of the house was not delivered. The

amount is to be refunded to the complainant. The OP would return the

entire amount receive by it along with interest @ 18% simple interest

from the dates of deposits till its realization."
14.
In
Arvinder Singh Vs. Unitech Hi-Tech Developers Limited

& Anr.
2016 (3) CLT 339, Hon'ble National Commission has observed

that "possession of flat was not delivered to the complainant for five

years. The builder has been directed to refund amount along with
 // 13 //

interest @ 18% per annum from the respective dates of payment of

these amounts till their realization."
15. In K.A. Nagamani Vs. Housing Commissioner, Karnataka

Housing Board, III (2016) CPJ 16 (SC), Hon'ble Supreme Court has

observed that "Allotment of flat - Consideration deposited - Non -

construction of flat on ground that dispute raised by land owners

pending before Court - Refund of amount after 14 years - Deficiency

in service - Complainant succeeded in showing deficiency in part of

respondent which was also accepted by State Commission- In spite of

such finding, no separate compensation was allowed in favour of

complainant. Though State Commission failed to exercise its

jurisdiction and proceeded with material irregularity, National

Commission erred in holding that petition was not maintainable and

wrongly imposed cost on complainant - Amount was simply returned

and complainant is suffering a loss inasmuch as she had deposited the

money in the hope of getting a flat but she is being deprived of benefit

of escalation of price of that flat - Respondent is directed to pay

complainant interest @ 18% p.a. on deposited amount - Compensation

@ Rs.50,000/- awarded - Cost Rs.20,000/- awarded.
16. In the instant case also, the OPs received entire amount of

Rs.22,35,000/- from the complainant but the OPs did not construct the

flat and did not deliver possession of the flat to the complainant.
// 14 //

According to the agreement, the complainant is entitled for refund of

the amount deposited by him with the OPs with adequate

compensation. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, it is

just and proper to direct the OPs to refund the amount of

Rs.22,35,000/- to the complainant along with interest 18% p.a. interest

from 30.10.2012 till realisation.
17. The complaint sought a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards

compensation for mental agony. It is established that the complainant

deposited the entire consideration amount of the flat in question to the

OPs, but the OPs did not construct the flat. The licence issued by

Town and Country Planning Department, Raipur has been cancelled

by the Government. The charge sheet has been filed against builder.

Certainly the complainant would have suffered mental agony, but

Rs.5,00,000/- is on higher side. It is just and proper to award a sum of

Rs.2,00,000/- towards compensation for mental agony to the

complainant.
18. Therefore, the complaint of the complainant is allowed and it

is directed that :-
(i) The OPs will jointly and severally pay within two

 months from the date of this order a sum of Rs.22,35,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Two Lakhs Thirty Five Thousand) to the
 // 15 //

complainant along with interest @ 18% p.a. from 30.10.2012 till

realisation.
(ii) The OPs will jointly and severally pay a sum of

Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs) to the complainant towards

compensation for mental agony.
(iii) The OPs will jointly and severally pay a sum of

Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) towards cost of litigation to

the complainant.
(Justice R.S. Sharma) (D.K. Poddar)
